---
title: "4.4 Assumptions"
order: 4
---

Four assumptions carry the model. For each: what it is, the evidence, and what breaks if
it fails. Two hold, one holds only in part, and one cannot be tested with the data the
model was built on.

## Monotonic weight of evidence

**The assumption.** For each numeric feature, risk moves one way across its range: more
leverage, more risk; longer history, less. A scorecard whose WoE rises and falls across a
feature's bins gives an applicant a better score for a worse value somewhere in the range,
and a reason code that cannot be defended.

**The evidence.** `train.py` does not constrain the direction: `BinningProcess` is called
without a `monotonic_trend`, so `optbinning` uses its default, `"auto"`, which chooses a
shape per feature and may choose one that is not monotonic. Read in bin order, the WoE of
{{< var score.n_woe_nonmonotonic >}} of the {{< var score.n_numeric >}} numeric features is
not monotonic: **{{< var score.woe_nonmonotonic >}}**. The binning tables show it:

```python
scorecard.binning_process_.get_binned_variable("leverage").binning_table.build()
```

`leverage` enters the generator's default logit with one sign
(`shared/data_generator.py`), so the break in its WoE is most likely sampling noise that
the binning kept. `trade_lines` has no role in the generator at all, so any shape its WoE takes is
noise; it is part of finding 3 ([4.7](limitations.qmd)).

**What breaks if it fails.** Not discrimination: the held-out AUC in
[4.5](performance.qmd) is measured with these bins. What breaks is defensibility, for the
applicants whose values fall where the WoE turns. The assumption **holds in part**. It is
finding 5 in [4.7](limitations.qmd), with its control: set the monotonic trend explicitly
for each numeric feature at redevelopment.

## Feature independence

**The assumption.** No feature is so well predicted by the others that the regression
cannot separate their effects. If one were, its coefficient would be unstable, and could
even take the wrong sign.

**The evidence**, on the WoE columns of the training split:

| Measure | Value | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Largest pairwise correlation (absolute) | {{< var score.corr_max >}} | {{< var score.corr_max_pair >}} |
| Largest variance inflation factor | {{< var score.vif_max >}} | {{< var score.vif_max_feature >}} |

The largest correlation is built in: `revenue_per_employee` is `annual_revenue` divided by
`employees` (`compute_features`). The decisive check is the coefficients' signs: all
{{< var score.n_features >}} are {{< var score.coef_sign >}} (opposite-signed:
{{< var score.coef_opposite >}}; [4.3](methodology.qmd#coefficient-signs)). No effect
has been flipped by collinearity. The assumption **holds**.

**What breaks if it fails.** The reason codes: with collinear features, WoE × coefficient
splits one effect between two features arbitrarily.

## A stable population

**The assumption.** The applicants the model scores look like the ones it was fitted on.

**The evidence.** Between the training and held-out splits, the score-band PSI is
{{< var score.psi_score >}}; the largest feature PSI is {{< var score.psi_max >}}
(on {{< var score.psi_max_feature >}}), and {{< var score.psi_n_over_010 >}} features exceed
the {{< var monitoring.psi_watch >}} watch level ([4.5](performance.qmd#stability)). But
the two splits are a random partition of **one cross-section** of applicants. Their PSI
measures sampling noise, not drift over time. There is no out-of-time sample, so the
assumption is **untested** — finding 1 ([4.7](limitations.qmd)), controlled by the
monitoring plan ([4.8](monitoring.qmd)).

**What breaks if it fails.** Both the ranking and the PD: bins fitted on one population
misplace applicants from a shifted one, and the PD in each band drifts from the rate
actually observed.

## The generator as ground truth

**The assumption.** The data generator's outcomes are the truth the model is measured
against. Every `default` in the data was drawn by `shared/data_generator.py`, with noise
added twice: inside the default logit, and again in the draw of each outcome from its
probability.

**The evidence.** The generator is code, so the truth is known exactly. That is what lets
[4.5](performance.qmd#the-ceiling) state the best AUC any model could reach on this data,
and [4.7](limitations.qmd) say which features have no causal role. The same fact bounds
every claim in this chapter: each is a statement about the generator, not about any real
book ([D1](../d1-purpose.qmd#scope-synthetic-data-real-methods)).

**What breaks if it fails.** On real data there is no generator to consult: the ceiling
and the structural-zero findings could not be established, and would have to be argued
from domain knowledge and out-of-time evidence instead.
